title: Grok Requirements (Admin-Pinned Config Patch)
description: `requirements.toml` is NOT an independently-modeled format: it shares `config.toml`'s exact TOML section/key namespace (`[features]`, `[telemetry]`, `[cli]`, `[memory]`, `[subagents]`, `[managed_mcps]`, `[tools]`, `[ui]`, `[models]`, `[endpoints]`, `[sandbox]`, `[mcp]`, …) as an OPTIONAL-EVERYTHING patch — every accessor in `apply_requirements_inner`/`resolve/*.rs` reads it with the identical `req.get("<section>")?.get("<key>")?.as_bool()`/`as_str()` pattern used for `config.toml`'s own sections. This schema is therefore a THIN WRAPPER over `grok-config.schema.json` (all its fields, all optional) plus exactly two requirements-only extension keys stripped before the rest of the table is treated as a config patch: `fail_closed` and `[[version_overrides]]`. Sources, in load order (later wins on key conflict via `deep_merge_toml`): (1) `$GROK_HOME/requirements.toml` (typically `~/.grok/requirements.toml`, user-writable, `is_system: false`); (2) `/etc/grok/requirements.toml` (`is_system: true`); (3) macOS MDM managed preferences, domain `ai.x.grok`, key `requirements_toml_base64` — admin-*forced* values only, no file on disk, `is_system: true`, decoded standard-base64 -> UTF-8 -> TOML -> non-empty table, used VERBATIM (`${VAR}`/`$VAR` are deliberately NOT env-expanded in this tier, unlike file layers, so the excluded local user can't influence the trusted layer via their own environment). [src: crates/codegen/xai-grok-config/src/validation.rs:66-124; crates/codegen/xai-grok-config/src/macos_managed.rs:8-40]

fail_closed.description: Requirements-only top-level extension key (NOT part of config.toml's namespace). Defined OUTSIDE this crate/workspace-tree, in the cross-crate `prod/mc/cli-chat-proxy-types` package: `pub const FAIL_CLOSED_KEY: &str = "fail_closed";` with parse helper `fail_closed_flag_status_from_value` returning `FailClosedFlag::{True, False, Invalid}` — absent key -> `False`; a non-bool value (e.g. `fail_closed = "true"`) -> `Invalid`, treated as `false` with a one-time `tracing::warn!`, never a hard error by itself. `fail_closed` is ALWAYS stripped from the layer's value before it's used as a config-merge patch (`table.remove(FAIL_CLOSED_KEY)`) — it never leaks into the effective merged config seen by consumers. When true (possibly tightened, never loosened, by the `GROK_MANAGED_CONFIG_FAIL_CLOSED` env var), a bad `[[version_overrides]]` semver in this same layer becomes a fatal `RequirementsError::InvalidVersionOverrides` at startup validation instead of a soft-skip. [src: prod/mc/cli-chat-proxy-types/src/deployment_config_types.rs:110; crates/codegen/xai-grok-config/src/validation.rs:12-26,143-145,186-244]

version_overrides.description: Requirements-only top-level extension key `[[version_overrides]]` (array of tables, NOT part of config.toml's namespace) — `VERSION_OVERRIDES_KEY = "version_overrides"`. Each element's `minimum_version`/`maximum_version` are pulled out as typed meta; the REST of that table's keys/values are an arbitrary TOML patch, deep-merged onto the requirements value when the running CLI's semver falls within `[minimum_version, maximum_version]` (both bounds inclusive; on a tie in `minimum_version`, later-declared entries win). An invalid semver in either bound is a hard error (`VersionOverrideError::InvalidMinimumVersion`/`InvalidMaximumVersion`) regardless of `fail_closed` — `fail_closed` only controls whether that error aborts the layer (soft-skip) or is propagated as fatal at CLI startup. `version_overrides` is ALWAYS stripped from the layer after processing, win or no match. [src: crates/codegen/xai-grok-config/src/version_overrides.rs:1-30,54-106,140-143]

items.description: One `[[version_overrides]]` array element. `minimum_version`/`maximum_version` are typed via `VersionOverrideMeta`; every other key/value in this table is an arbitrary config-patch fragment applied when the semver gate matches (e.g. `[version_overrides.features]` etc.) — hence no `additionalProperties: false` here, ever. [src: crates/codegen/xai-grok-config/src/version_overrides.rs:24-30]

minimum_version.description: Inclusive lower-bound semver string for this override to apply. `#[serde(default)] Option<String>` — missing means no lower bound (effectively `"0.0.0"`). An invalid semver string is a hard error. [src: crates/codegen/xai-grok-config/src/version_overrides.rs:26-27]

maximum_version.description: Inclusive upper-bound semver string for this override to apply. `#[serde(default)] Option<String>` — missing means no upper bound. An invalid semver string is a hard error. [src: crates/codegen/xai-grok-config/src/version_overrides.rs:28-29]
